🇲🇽🏥 <u>ISSSTE: 12 Actions in 120 Days</u>

Martí Batres laid out ISSSTE's 120-day plan at the mañanera: hire 1,710 specialists, 502 nurses and 250 general practitioners, finish seven hospital and clinic projects, and keep the medicine supply above 97%. The plan also covers 55 rehabilitated operating rooms, 100 new consultorios for the Universal Health Service, and overhauls of the Darío Fernández hospital in CDMX and the Manuel Cárdenas de la Vega hospital in Culiacán. The Oaxaca high-specialty hospital is already 89% complete.

🇲🇽🥑 <u>Mexico Shields Its Avocado From the Borer Worm</u>

Mexico's Agriculture Ministry (Sader) inspected 1,774 avocado shipments between August 13 and October 30, covering 7,391 tons, to keep the borer worm out of protected zones like Michoacán. When two infested loads turned up on October 28, one was sent back and the other destroyed, and 52 tons of fruit were destroyed across Michoacán, Jalisco, Colima and Nayarit. Five checkpoints (Apatzingán, Buenavista, Cotija, Jiquilpan and Zamora) guard the export heartland of the world's top avocado producer.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Sheinbaum Skips Madrid, Eyes APEC in China</u>

Sheinbaum won't attend the Ibero-American Summit in Madrid on November 4-5. Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco will lead Mexico's delegation, and the President's November calendar points to the APEC summit in China. She isn't the only one: Lula and Venezuela's Delcy Rodríguez are also sending their foreign ministers, so only 10 of 22 heads of state and government will be in Madrid.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexico and the US Settle the Tecnos Labor Case Without a T-MEC Panel</u>

Mexico and the United States signed a memorandum of understanding on November 2 that closes the labor dispute at Industrias Tecnos, an ammunition plant in Cuernavaca, Morelos, and stops the arbitration panel Washington had requested under the T-MEC. The company must pay legal compensation for wages and benefits owed to dismissed workers, train staff on union neutrality and set up a confidential complaints channel. Mexico's labor authorities will review the dismissals, inspect the plant and run in-person courses on union rights. The case had been open since May 2024, El Economista reports. Of the six panels requested against Mexico, only Pirelli and Bader remain under review.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>SEP Answers El Universal: Dropout Rate Is Falling, Not Rising</u>

El Universal ran a headline saying the 4T's scholarships "drive students away," built on a UNESCO report that re-cited a study on the end of Prospera in 2019. Mexico's Education Ministry (SEP) answered with the numbers: the high-school dropout rate fell from 14.5% in 2017-2018 to 9.3% in 2024-2025. Becas para el Bienestar now reach more than 19.5 million students, with 136.9 billion pesos invested this year. More than 1.8 million students signed up for the universal Benito Juárez high-school scholarship for 2026-2027, up from an average of 1.5 million.

🇲🇽👵 <u>One in Every Four Pesos Mexico Spends Goes to Pensions</u>

Through September, Mexico's federal government spent 1.742 trillion pesos on pensions, 24% of all public spending, according to Hacienda. That covers contributory pensions and the universal pensions for everyone over 65 and for women aged 60 to 64. In 2015 pension spending was about 630 billion pesos, 3.4% of GDP. This year it reaches roughly 2.3 trillion, 6% of GDP.

🇲🇽📵 <u>Phones Out of Mexican Classrooms Starting Today</u>

As of today, November 3, cellphone use is restricted during class and recess in every public and private primary and secondary school in Mexico. Students can keep their phones in their backpacks for emergencies. High schools will set their own rules with teachers and parents, and universities will teach digital citizenship: critical thinking, how algorithms and screens work, and AI. Education Secretary Mario Delgado's SEP is filling the breaks with board games, reading and sports instead.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Pemex exports 32% less crude but earns more</u>

In September Pemex shipped just 389,000 barrels a day abroad, 31.8% less than a year earlier. Export revenue still rose 2.4%, to $1.062 billion, because the average Mexican export price hit $91 a barrel, its highest since July 2022 (El Financiero). In May it took 513,300 barrels a day to bring in $1.41 billion. The crude that stays home goes to Mexican refineries, which processed 1.143 million barrels a day in Q3, the most since 2014.

🇲🇽🚆 <u>Tren Maya passes 3 million passengers</u>

The train the opposition spent years trying to stop with court injunctions has now carried more than 3 million passengers since it began running on December 15, 2023. Tourism Secretary Josefina Rodríguez Zamora announced the milestone. The line links Chiapas, Tabasco, Campeche, Yucatán and Quintana Roo, and Sectur is now promoting it at trade fairs and tourism caravans in the United States and Canada.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexico completes FATF anti-money-laundering review</u>

Mexico has completed its Mutual Evaluation by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF/GAFI), whose plenary closed on October 30, and it remains off both the FATF black list and the grey list. The UIF led the process, coordinating Banxico, the FGR, the CNBV, Defense, the National Guard, the SRE and the National Intelligence Center, along with the banks. The full report, with technical-compliance and effectiveness ratings, will be published on December 17.
